partTypes.name: Extracellular space
partTypes.description: The world outside the cell. Its concentrations are fixed for the level — connect channels to it to exchange molecules.

partTypes.name: Cytoplasm
partTypes.description: The cell body. Everything else connects back to it.

partTypes.name: Mitochondrion
partTypes.description: Burns glucose and oxygen to make ATP, and produces waste doing it.

partTypes.name: Ribosome
partTypes.description: Spends ATP to build biomass. This is what actually keeps the cell alive.

partTypes.name: Peroxisome
partTypes.description: Breaks down waste directly, no substrate needed — an organelle slot spent on detox instead of a membrane pump.

partTypes.name: Biosynthesis complex
partTypes.description: Spends glucose AND ATP together to build biomass directly — a second claim on the same pools the mitochondrion and ribosome already draw from.

partTypes.name: Organelle membrane
partTypes.description: Connects an organelle to the cytoplasm so molecules can equilibrate between them.

partTypes.name: Glucose channel
partTypes.description: A passive channel letting glucose diffuse down its concentration gradient.

partTypes.name: Oxygen channel
partTypes.description: A passive channel letting oxygen diffuse down its concentration gradient.

partTypes.name: Waste channel
partTypes.description: A passive channel letting waste diffuse down its concentration gradient.

partTypes.name: Glucose transporter (active)
partTypes.description: Vesicle-mediated active transport: pulls a fixed amount of glucose in per tick, even against the gradient, as long as the environment has any left.

partTypes.name: Efflux pump (active)
partTypes.description: Actively pumps waste out of the cell at a fixed rate, even into a toxic, waste-saturated environment.
